Alex / team,

Technical detail below (long):
1) Deletion workflow summary:
   - User/API issues delete -> object marked with tombstone in primary metadata store (near-immediate).
   - Tombstone is published to the replication queue (Kafka topic) per volume/shard.
   - Replica ingestion picks up tombstone and marks the object as deleted locally (metadata-only) immediately upon consumption.
   - Expunge job runs in waves (configurable TTL) and removes data blobs after the legal-retention window finishes.

2) Timelines (typical cluster config we run for Dedicated/Private customers):
   - Best case: tombstone observed on replica within < 1 minute (low queue depth, no backlog).
   - Typical: 1-30 minutes (normal replication latency + small backlog windows).
   - Conservative worst case: up to 72 hours (very high replication backlog, ongoing region maintenance, or cross-region throttling during heavy churn).

3) Common causes of delay:
   - Backfill/replication backlog after an outage (we prioritize data durability; backlog drains at controlled rate).
   - KMS key unavailability or rotation windows where encrypted blob rekeys are pending — tombstone is still applied to metadata but blob expunge may be delayed if re-encryption is in-flight.
   - Manual retention overrides or legal holds prevent expunge (even though tombstone exists).
   - Long-running cold-archive tier migrations where physical deletion is batched.

4) What to look for in logs / evidence:
   - Tombstone publish entries: replication_topic.partition.<id> offset and timestamp.
   - Replica ingestion acknowledgement: replica.<region>.ingest.tombstone.<object_id> entries.
   - Expunge job run logs: expunge.wave.<id> start/end and removed_blob.<object_id> entries.
   - KMS events: key.version.rotate and key.access.fail.

5) For your CSV case: if the primary shows delete at 2026-03-08T22:04:12Z and replica still had blob present at 2026-03-09T10:30Z, two likely scenarios: backlog while we drained after maintenance, or the object had a retention override. If you can share the Request IDs I can correlate the replication_topic offsets and paste the exact ingestion acknowledgement.
